description: Synthetic, credential-free Codex sessions whose next-task queries deliberately use different wording from the durable learning event.

sessions.trigger: A lifecycle callback delayed agent shutdown while it performed several network requests.
sessions.conclusion: Send one bounded batch to the known capture endpoint during the stop callback.
sessions.rationale: Discovery and per-item requests multiply tail latency after useful work has already completed.
sessions.reuse_rule: For termination callbacks, skip capability discovery, cap the payload at three items, and enforce a five-second deadline.
sessions.outcome: The callback completed within its latency budget without duplicate submissions.
queries: How should an agent avoid hanging after it has already finished its work?
What pattern reduces end-of-run network chatter in a lifecycle integration?

sessions.trigger: Dependency installation failed because the package-manager launcher could not validate its signed release metadata.
sessions.conclusion: Restore a trusted Corepack and package-manager installation instead of bypassing signature verification.
sessions.rationale: Disabling integrity checks makes a transient toolchain problem indistinguishable from a compromised artifact.
sessions.reuse_rule: When package bootstrap reports key or signature errors, repair the trusted launcher and keep verification enabled.
sessions.outcome: The pinned package manager executed the test suite with integrity validation intact.
queries: The JavaScript dependency bootstrap says its signing key is invalid; what is the safe recovery?
Should supply-chain verification be switched off just to get the build running?

sessions.trigger: A privacy filter classified dates, timestamps, and long platform identifiers as telephone numbers.
sessions.conclusion: Recognize structured numeric identifiers before applying phone-number detection.
sessions.rationale: Digit count alone cannot distinguish personal contact data from ISO dates or service-generated IDs.
sessions.reuse_rule: Exclude known date, timestamp, and status-ID formats, then apply the contact-number detector to the remainder.
sessions.outcome: Regression fixtures retained identifiers while still rejecting actual contact numbers.
queries: Why is the privacy scrubber deleting harmless calendar values and social post references?
How can numeric false positives be reduced without weakening protection for contact details?

sessions.trigger: A maintenance job needed to suppress and reclassify every stored memory.
sessions.conclusion: Require a restorable snapshot and checksum manifest before applying bulk repair.
sessions.rationale: A dry run describes intended mutations but cannot recover data after an interrupted or incorrect apply.
sessions.reuse_rule: Before mass maintenance, create a permission-restricted database copy or export and verify its digest.
sessions.outcome: The repair completed with every original identifier recoverable.
queries: What safety gate is mandatory before rewriting the entire knowledge store?
A cleanup preview looks correct; what additional protection is needed before committing it?

sessions.trigger: Semantic indexing failed because the inference output width did not match the configured vector index.
sessions.conclusion: Validate every embedding dimension before persisting or querying it.
sessions.rationale: Model variants and truncation settings can silently change vector shape while storage expects a fixed width.
sessions.reuse_rule: Pin model and dimensions together, reject non-finite values, and fail before writing mismatched vectors.
sessions.outcome: Both document and query vectors were consistently stored at 1024 dimensions.
queries: Why does similarity lookup reject arrays produced by a newly selected language model?
Which invariant prevents an inference backend from corrupting the nearest-neighbor index?

sessions.trigger: A serverless API exhausted memory while serializing a very large memory-list response.
sessions.conclusion: Use cursor pagination and a compact projection for high-cardinality lists.
sessions.rationale: Bounding rows and omitting large evidence bodies prevents response assembly from exceeding runtime memory limits.
sessions.reuse_rule: Offer full pages up to one hundred rows and compact pages up to five hundred rows with an opaque continuation cursor.
sessions.outcome: Repeated list requests completed without platform resource errors.
queries: How should a serverless endpoint return thousands of records without running out of memory?
What response design avoids oversized administrative table payloads?

sessions.trigger: A previously verified lesson referred to source code that had changed since capture.
sessions.conclusion: Do not inject a file-backed memory when its recorded content hash no longer matches the workspace.
sessions.rationale: A correct historical conclusion may become unsafe after the implementation it describes is revised.
sessions.reuse_rule: Recompute referenced file hashes at retrieval time and route mismatches to stale review.
sessions.outcome: Outdated guidance was withheld until it was reverified against current code.
queries: When should previously trusted engineering guidance be withheld after a refactor?
How can retrieval detect that remembered advice no longer describes the checked-out implementation?

sessions.trigger: An otherwise useful learning event contained an authentication secret in command output.
sessions.conclusion: Reject credentials unconditionally before memory persistence.
sessions.rationale: Access controls and short retention reduce exposure but do not make reusable secret storage safe.
sessions.reuse_rule: Detect keys, tokens, passwords, and private-key material before logging or capture, and record only a reason code.
sessions.outcome: No secret value entered memory, logs, or diagnostic reports.
queries: Can a short-lived restricted note retain an API password for future agents?
What should the capture pipeline do when useful output is mixed with authentication material?

sessions.trigger: An automatically inferred architectural rule was considered for pre-action blocking.
sessions.conclusion: Allow an unconfirmed inferred decision to block only with high confidence and independently verified evidence.
sessions.rationale: A confident statement without corroboration can still be fabricated or based on stale context.
sessions.reuse_rule: Require explicit decision language, rationale, matching scope, no unresolved conflict, and at least one admissible execution or source attestation.
sessions.outcome: Unsupported guidance went to review while strongly evidenced constraints were enforced.
queries: When may machine-inferred policy stop an engineer before an action is taken?
Why should a very confident recommendation still be advisory when nothing corroborates it?

sessions.trigger: A hook retried delivery after timing out and created multiple copies of the same lesson.
sessions.conclusion: Derive stable canonical and event keys so repeated capture is idempotent.
sessions.rationale: Network retry is normal and must not inflate retrieval results with semantically identical rows.
sessions.reuse_rule: Hash tenant, project, kind, and normalized conclusion for canonical identity, then combine it with the event identifier.
sessions.outcome: Retries updated or skipped the existing memory instead of creating active duplicates.
queries: How can retrying a timed-out knowledge submission avoid producing twins?
What identity scheme makes repeated lifecycle delivery safe?

sessions.trigger: Captured memories were assigned inconsistent categories by guessing from their prose.
sessions.conclusion: Derive category deterministically from explicit project metadata, never from memory text.
sessions.rationale: The same technical statement can occur in many projects, so content inference makes routing unstable.
sessions.reuse_rule: Prefer explicit classification, then workspace configuration, then a hashed project category; reject invalid explicit values.
sessions.outcome: Local and cloud captures received identical stable classifications.
queries: How should a knowledge item be classified when its wording could belong to several teams?
What prevents categorization from changing when the same lesson is paraphrased?

sessions.trigger: Integration tests depended on a developer's globally running inference service.
sessions.conclusion: Own the local model process inside the test runner and terminate it in a finally block.
sessions.rationale: Global daemons make tests order-dependent and leave machine state behind after failures.
sessions.reuse_rule: Allocate a loopback port, start the service, wait for health, run the suite, and send termination even when tests fail.
sessions.outcome: The embedding regression ran from a clean machine state and left no service listening afterward.
queries: How can integration checks avoid relying on a manually launched model server?
What teardown pattern prevents a failed test from leaving an inference process behind?
